newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chatichai given major concession. The Chart Pattana leader won a major concession in overseeing economic affairs yesterday after the Prime Minister agreed to let him chair meetings of the government's economic advisory teams every Thursday.

Chavalit Yonchaiyudh yielded to Chatichai Choonhavan's party in a move to tame dissent among Chart Pattana members who say Amnauy Viravan, the Finance Minister, is monopolising economic management, sources said. (BANGKOK POST)

-Foreign investors flock to swap stocks for baht. Volume on the Thai bouse surged abnormally yesterday to above Bt10 billion as foreign investors frantically arbitraged between the stock mrket and the foreign exchange market to get their hands on baht and re-lend it in the offshore market at interest rates of 55 to 100 percent, analysts said.
The currency arbitrage follows the central bank's decision to shut down the foreign exchange swap market to punish currency speculators who attacked the baht in mid-May. (THE NATION)
- Baht defence rebounds on SET. Efforts to ward off speculative attacks on the baht are buffeting the already battered Stock Exchange of Thailand.

Investors are dumping shares, taking the proceeds out of Thailand, and then repatriating them in dollars after benefiting from the favourable offshore exchange rates, dealers and analysts said yesterday. (BUSINESS POST)

- Amnuay tries to save new bank's licence. Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said yesterday the authorities will allow Italian-Thai Development and MBK Property to restructure their shareholdings by seeking mergers with finance companies before applying for a renewal of their bank licenses.

The two companies had sought to relax the regulations applying to their initial public offerings because the present market environment would not permit them to raise the Bt7.5 billion captial needed to fulfil the new banking requirements. (THE NATION BUSINESS)
